DECISION_LOG.md: no row for any --ngram-ve-dim, --ngram-ve-table-mult, or other n-gram capacity setting at 9a4caa7b; only --no-ngram-ve (smoke only, no verdict row) and --ngram-rms-fp32 (precision, DISCARD smoke) touch the n-gram path
expected_effect: Predicted: candidate steps +6% to +12% versus same-host control (about 2200-2320 steps) and public_val_bpb lower than same-host control by 0.001 to 0.004 (roughly 1.0020-1.0047 on trn22 scale). If the halved width costs more than the extra steps buy, BPB will be >= control despite >= +3% steps (FALSIFIED-CAPACITY).
hypothesis: At the pinned defaults the four hashed n-gram value-embedding tables (rows=1048576, dim=128, 4 tables = ~537M of the 592.9M parameters; core model is ~55.7M per the --no-ngram-ve smoke row) dominate per-step parameter traffic (gather, RMSprop update, and gradient reduction across the 4 ranks). The --no-ngram-ve smoke shows that removing them entirely raises the 300 s step count from 334-335 to 410 (~+22%) but costs ~+0.008 BPB at smoke horizon, so the tables carry real information. Halving the table width to dim=64 should recover a substantial fraction of that step-rate headroom (predicted +6% to +12% steps in 1800 s) while retaining most of the n-gram information (address space and number of tables unchanged; only the per-slot vector width halves). Because the only 30-minute win at this commit (--bf16-sdpa-input: 2233 vs 2076 steps, 1.002028 vs 1.005967) came from a throughput lever with unchanged capacity, a throughput lever with a mild capacity reduction is predicted to net a lower public_val_bpb than control.
single_causal_change: Pass --ngram-ve-dim 64 only. Every other option stays at the 9a4caa7b defaults used by the two pinned controls: identical launch shape (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2, torchrun --nproc_per_node=4, --num-steps 5000, --max-train-seconds 1800, --seed 42), identical environment (NEURON_CC_FLAGS exactly '--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1). No precision flag (no --bf16-sdpa-input, --bf16-norm-output, --ngram-rms-fp32), no kernel flag (no --nki-*), no --compile-* change, no other ngram-ve option (--ngram-ve stays on; tables, rows/table-mult, trigram, opt=rmsprop, flat_lr, bf16, clip-exclude, layers, lr, beta2 all untouched), no optimizer/schedule/batch/architecture/evaluation change. The only behavioral delta is the per-slot width of the hashed n-gram value-embedding tables: 128 -> 64. Pre-full checks: the candidate's resolved ngram_ve oneliner must read 'True tables=4 rows=1048576 dim=64 ...' (controls read dim=128) and reported num_params_M must fall to roughly 55.7 + 4*1048576*64/1e6 ~ 324M (+/- a few M for any dim-dependent projection). If the oneliner still shows dim=128 or the run fails to construct the model, classify NOT-EXERCISED and do not spend the full run. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 -> 2071 steps / 1.005734; trn22 -> 2076 steps / 1.005967). Related, distinguished evidence: al-20260922-no-ngram-ve-only-default-shape-smoke-r1 (trn21, 410 steps, 1.173413) tests total removal; this proposal tests the intermediate width and is predicted to land between control and the no-ngram-ve arm on both steps and BPB. Outcome classes, mutually exclusive, evaluated in order: (1) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if candidate steps < 90% of same-host control steps (experiment-protocol.md section 5; record as throughput regression only); (2) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-1% of control and |delta BPB| < 0.0005 (width change did not alter throughput or quality); (3) SUCCESS if steps >= control and public_val_bpb <= same-host control - 0.001; (4) FALSIFIED-CAPACITY if steps >= +3% of control but public_val_bpb >= same-host control (throughput gained, but halved n-gram width lost more than it bought); (5) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (small step gain and/or |delta BPB| < 0.001).
